findings.title: Four 1,668-1,940-line prelude-dispatch matches chained via trailing wildcards forfeit exhaustiveness and are order-dependent across files
findings.description: lower_prelude_type_instance_fn_arms (instance_fns.rs:24-1882, 1,884-line file) delegates via `_ =>` to instance_fns_extra.rs:23 (1,700 lines); lower_prelude_type_assoc_fn (prelude_types.rs:58, 1,940-line file) delegates at :1812 to framework.rs:31 (1,697 lines). A new PreludeInstanceFn/PreludeAssocFn variant fails at codegen-runtime ('unsupported') instead of compile-time non-exhaustive-match. Worse: negative-guard catch-alls placed mid-chain preempt specific arms in the SIBLING FILE (instance_fns.rs:1012 `M::Len if !Cache|String` must stay before extra's String:1009/Cache:299; Tensor Len :72 fires before shared Len; comment at :1006-1011 documents this cross-file coupling). Reordering or splitting further silently changes semantics.
findings.root_cause: ITER-31..44 mechanical file splits cut one giant match into 4 files preserving order via trailing wildcards instead of restructuring into a table/exhaustive-per-type dispatch.
findings.impact: Compiler's most-extended seam (every T124 stdlib task) silently degrades: missing arms surface as user-facing codegen errors, not developer-time compile errors; arm insertion requires reasoning about guard ordering in 2 files.
findings.recommendation: Extract per-(Type,fn) dispatch into a static table keyed by (PreludeType, PreludeInstanceFn) -> handler fn, with per-file registration; or split by PreludeType (not by arm count) so each match remains exhaustive within one file; add a debug_assert test enumerating all enum variants against the table.
fix_guide: Define Handler = fn(&mut RustCodegen,&Type,SynExpr,&[Expr])->Result<SynExpr,CodegenError>
Register existing arms per (recv_ty, variant) key in per-domain modules (datetime.rs, tensor.rs, ...); drop all negative guards
Add a #[test] that iterates strum::EnumIter over both enums asserting full key coverage
Migrate arm-by-arm keeping byte-identical snapshot output green between commits

effort_estimate.breakdown: 240 handler extraction+registration, 120 table infra, 120 variant-coverage test, 480 snapshot re-validation across 120 snapshots

detection_method.query: line counts of the 4 fns + trailing wildcard `_ => self.lower_..._extra` + M::Len guard grep

references: crates/buff-lang-codegen-rust/AGENTS.md (documents the split as verbatim move but not the exhaustiveness forfeiture)

confidence.rationale: All 4 file sizes, both wildcard sites, and all guard line numbers directly read; AGENTS.md itself describes the ordered-wildcard chain

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: The _extra file split itself IS a documented verbatim move (not flagged); the finding targets the wildcard-chain semantics and cross-file guard ordering, which no convention doc declares deliberate

The in-file generic program_uses_namespace(:1455) plus one-liner wrappers program_uses_base64/hex/percent_encoding/uuid/url (:1600-1636) prove the predicate-parameterized walker is feasible and already adopted for the newest crates.
findings.root_cause: Walkers were copy-pasted per crate before the generic namespace walker was written; legacy families were never migrated.

findings.recommendation: Re-express the 8 legacy walkers as one-liners delegating to program_uses_namespace or a small predicate-closure variant; keep public names stable so registration code is untouched.
fix_guide: For each legacy walker, grep which Buff namespaces/types trigger it (see extern_crate_registration.rs)

findings.title: isNull() unconditionally panics, isNotNull() is an empty no-op, matches() silently does substring matching
findings.description: In impl<T: Debug> AssertThat<T>: isNull() (:104-112) panics unconditionally even when called on Option<T> (the Option-specific impl at :121 adds isSome/isNone but no isNull override), so null-ness is unassertable. isNotNull() (:114-118) has an EMPTY body â€” it can never fail, so `assertThat(x).isNotNull()` is a test that always passes. matches() (:170-178) delegates to str::contains, so `matches("a.c")` passes on 'abc' and 'aXc' alike â€” regex semantics implied by the name are absent. All three are absent from the README API table (as are isInstanceOf), so users hit the traps at runtime.
findings.root_cause: Placeholder stubs shipped in the T38 MVP and never finished; matches() copied contains() body.
findings.impact: False-confidence test passes (isNotNull) and unusable/false-failing API (isNull, matches) in the crate whose entire purpose is trustworthy assertions.
findings.recommendation: Implement isNotNull as `if self.actual is None panic` semantics via Debug-format guard (or make it Option-aware), implement isNull for Option<T> in the Option impl, and make matches() use the regex crate (add workspace regex dep) or rename to containsMatch.

fix_examples.before:
pub fn isNotNull(self) where T: fmt::Debug {
}

fix_guide: Move isNull/isNotNull into impl<T: Debug> AssertThat<Option<T>> with real checks; keep generic isNotNull as length/emptiness-agnostic non-empty check
Add regex workspace dep; matches() -> Regex::new(pattern).is_match(actual)
Add failing-path tests for all three; document methods in README table

effort_estimate.breakdown: 60 impl fixes, 30 regex wiring, 30 tests, 30 README/AGENTS sync

findings.title: Dummy scope-keeper functions exist solely to suppress unused-import warnings
findings.description: debug.rs:201-204 defines `_ensure_pathbuf_in_scope() -> PathBuf { PathBuf::new() }` under #[allow(dead_code)] with a comment admitting it exists to 'suppress unused-import warning for PathBuf when only Path is used at runtime'. backtrace.rs:173-176 repeats the pattern with _ensure_install_in_scope() calling install_panic_hook(). Zero-effect dead functions mask which imports are actually needed and defeat unused-import detection for the real code.
findings.root_cause: Import kept 'for forward-compat when --source-map is wired' (comment) instead of re-adding when needed.
findings.impact: Reader overhead and false signal that PathBuf/panic-hook are used; rustc's unused-import lint permanently disabled for those names in these modules.
findings.recommendation: Delete both fns and their imports; git history preserves them. If --source-map wiring lands, re-add the import then (compiler will demand it).

fix_examples.after: // (deleted; re-add `use std::path::PathBuf;` when --source-map wiring needs it)

fix_guide: Remove _ensure_pathbuf_in_scope + PathBuf import from debug.rs; cargo check
Remove _ensure_install_in_scope from backtrace.rs; cargo check
Run crate tests

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Comments self-identify as warning-suppression hacks; no convention sanctions dummy fns

findings.title: Arity helper closures threaded as a 4-tuple across file boundary solely to dodge clippy::too_many_arguments
findings.description: prelude_types.rs:1810-1811 comment admits 'The arity closures travel as one 4-tuple (clippy too_many_arguments counts self, so four separate closure params would trip it)'; the wildcard delegation at :1812-1817 passes (&one_arg, &no_args, &two_args, &n_args) into framework.rs:31 whose signature carries #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] at :14. The closures are identical arity-checking utilities needed by every arm, yet are param-threaded per call, coupling the two files' signatures.
findings.root_cause: Helpers are defined as local closures inside lower_prelude_type_assoc_fn instead of shared associated fns, so crossing the file seam requires passing them.
findings.impact: Every future framework sibling file must replicate the 4-tuple parameter; signature churn and a lint suppression at each seam.
findings.recommendation: Promote the four arity helpers to private free fns (or an ArityChecks struct) in a prelude_types/arity.rs module importable by both files; delete the tuple and the allow at framework.rs:14.

fix_examples.after:

fix_guide: Extract one_arg/no_args/two_args/n_args bodies into prelude_types/arity.rs as pub(super) fns taking (&mut self-ish context) as needed
Update framework.rs to import and call them; drop the 4-tuple param and the allow attribute
Run crate snapshot tests
